01 / INTRODUCING TASC+

From spacecraft geometry
to electrical behavior.

TASC is an AI-driven spacecraft charging app for rapid spacecraft charging analysis. It brings geometry, surface materials, electrical connections, environments, and numerical solvers into one engineering workflow.

Explore how a design charges, where differential potentials develop, and how material or electrical changes affect the result. Inspect the assumptions alongside the fields they produce.

TASC / AI-ASSISTED MODELING+

From an image to a model
you can inspect.

A saved lander example

Keep the conversation beside the model.

Ask about geometry, materials, and the next steps in model preparation within TASC’s AI Object Builder.

Start with a reference image or a description. TASC’s AI Object Builder supports interpreting geometry, reviewing assumptions, and refining a model before accepting it for further preparation.

EXAMPLE REQUEST
“Create a conceptual lander model from this reference image. List the scale and geometry assumptions, then prepare a surface mesh for review.”
Illustrative wording for this workflow.

  1. Interpret the reference.

    Identify visible shapes and supports. Record estimates for scale, depth, and features that the image does not resolve.

  2. Build and inspect.

    In this saved example, an AI-interpreted concept was compiled locally by TASC into a 23-component lander model.

  3. Mesh, then review.

    TASC converted the concept into surface elements. An analyst still needs to review the geometry, assign materials and conductors, and approve the model before analysis.

What this example establishes

The saved artifact uses approximate geometry and an assumed 1.8 m person for scale. Hidden structure and some exterior details are omitted. Material assignments are provisional, solver input is not approved, and no charging simulation was run.

METHODS MATTER

Engineering insight starts
with clear assumptions.

TASC combines independent numerical methods with traceable material data. Each solver has a defined scope; verification focuses on the quantities that matter to the analysis.

Surface charging & electrostatic fields+

Finite-element (MFEM) and boundary-element (BEM) methods support charging and field analysis. The documented MFEM charging path uses CPU Laplace electrostatics and analytic currents; volume plasma space charge, wakes, and plumes are outside that path’s current scope.

Internal dielectric charging+

Transient internal-charging calculations connect deposited charge, electrostatics, and electrical leakage. This is a separate analysis from spacecraft surface charging, with its own physical inputs and assumptions.

Material provenance & verification+

A versioned material catalog retains sources and data status. Analytical checks, convergence studies, and independent solver comparisons provide development evidence. Suitability for a particular engineering decision requires validation of that case and configuration.
